faces.f: His verdict is always guilty. His sentence is always death.

"Sheesh! How am I supposed to make a decent living around here?"
—Cabal grave robber
"All your steel won't protect you if your will is weak."

"Jharic returned from Grixis changed, a haunted look in her eyes. She destroyed them with an unholy glee that made me shudder."
—Knight-Captain Wyhorn
The murdered inhabitants of Hollowhenge impart to the living the terror they felt in death.
Many who cross Sorin's path come down with a sudden and fatal case of being-in-the-way-of-a-millennia-old-vampire.

"I need never remember my past associates, my victims, my mistakes. Innistrad preserves them all for me."
—Sorin Markov
A gwyllion's favorite trap is the vanity mirror. A bewitched piece of glass traps the looker's soul and does away with the body.
Knowledge demands sacrifice.

"My 'condition' is a trial. The weak are consumed by it. The strong transcend it."
—Sorin Markov
Plate mail, the skin of the chest, the rib cage, the heart—all useless against the mage who can reach directly for the soul.
Without the interfering hands of civilization, nature will always shape itself to its own needs.
With great power comes great risk of getting yourself killed.
Each small blaze she sets jogs her memory, letting her piece together the mystery of her own fiery end.

"They may show up with the wrong thigh bone or mandible, but they always show up."
—Zul Ashur, lich lord
Its fiery paws make it easy to track, which is very useful when you want to go in exactly the opposite direction.

"The day is mine! I sent three such creatures against my foe, then watched as my magefire popped her soldiers like overripe spleenfruits."
—Dobruk the Unstable, pyromancer

"Her voice is disaster, painful and final."
—Matoc, lavamancer
"There's no heron in the moon! It's a shrew, a five-legged shrew, with a voice like whispering thunder!"

"Behind every devil's mayhem lurks a demon's scheme."
—Rem Karolus, Blade of the Inquisitors
"Within blood is life. Within life is fire. Within fire is the path to our masters' glory!"

"Well, how could I know they'd explode?"
—Gregel, township militia
It's not just the wind. It's not all in your head. And it's *definitely* something to worry about.
Barbarians equate courage with the ability to endure pain.
"Avacyn has abandoned us! We have nothing left except what we can take!"
After millennia asleep, the Eldrazi had forgotten about Zendikar's fiery temper and dislike of strangers.
Innistrad pyromancers find their best raw materials in the fury of the dead.
Chaos does not choose its enemies.

"I've seen death before. My mother succumbing to illness, my comrades bleeding on the battlefield . . . But I'd never seen anything as dreadful as that."
—Taani, berserker of Etlan

"What good is your blade without your breath?"
—Greht, Gathan warlord

"Pained defiance or shameful surrender—every reaction is a pleasant surprise."
—Tibalt
"Enough!"
In the spirit of inquiry, Tibalt applied a battery of agony spells. They yielded nothing on the vampire's whereabouts, but the screams were reward enough.
Gyara Spearhurler would have been renowned for her deadly accuracy, if it weren't for her deadly accuracy.
A devil's hands are never idle.
A blazing sun that never sets.
He has nothing left but his resentment.

"It is hope, hooved and winged."
—Cymede, queen of Akros
His prowess gives the guildless hope that they can hold out against tyranny.
"Once more into Devil's Breach, soldiers. I want another devil tail for my collection."
The tips of her bolts are blunt, but her aim is deadly sharp.
"In memories, we can find our deepest reserves of strength."
Confront her, and feel the hooves of her steed. Ignore her, and feel the sting of her arrow.
Akros's greatest heroes are also its royalty.
The Dimir agents watched from the shadows. "Eight hours, and I've yet to see him blink," Nefara hissed. "I suggest we find another way in."
Entire platoons have mysteriously vanished from battle, leaving enemy weapons to slice through empty air.
She crushes darkness beneath her charger's hooves.

"A great siege is a banquet to him; a long and terrible battle, the most exquisite delicacy."
—*The Seer's Parables*
In times when freedom seems lost, great souls arise to reclaim it.

"No doubt the arbiters would put you away, after all the documents are signed. But I will have justice now."
—Alovnek, Boros guildmage
What self-indulgence tears down, discipline builds up again.
"My course is before me. There is nothing behind me."
Sometimes the greatest strength is the strength of conviction.

"What cannot be destroyed will be bound."
—Oath of Avacyn
"My faith is stronger than fang, claw, or mindless hunger."

"Boom! Boom! Boots the size of oxcarts, then an axe like a falling sun. Elves scattered. Trees scattered. Even the hills ran for the hills!"
—*Clachan Tales*
Though the old holy wards and roadside shrines have begun to fail, faith in Avacyn still holds true power.
"I am the rock of the polis. Death only strengthens me."

"There shall be a vast shout and then a vaster silence."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
Enter with merciful hearts. Exit with battle cries.

"Wood is wasted in the dirt."
—Orcish proverb
Even dragons fear its silken strands.
In a withered world, the scent of healthy prey is enough to drive a predator to frenzy.
"Any festival you can walk away from wasn't worth attending in the first place."
"Only the decadent think magic should be pristine and without cost."
It's no coincidence that the oldest trolls are also the angriest.
The best way to calm a rampaging ceratok is to wait until it dies of natural causes.
Some of the eleven minotaur clans of Mirtiin are expert crafters and learned philosophers. Others just like to hit stuff.
The snap of sinew. The crunch of bone. A cry for mercy. These are the music of the Gruul.

"He bears the marks of ages upon his skin, memories of dreams long dead and best left buried."
—*The Seer's Parables*
It speaks no commands but is always obeyed.

"The sky isn't falling—it's being thrown at us!"
—Otak, Tin Street shopkeep
The viashino had learned how to operate the rig through trial and error—mostly error.

"You don't find many old werewolf hunters."
—Paulin, trapper of Somberwald

"Who'd want to ignite things one at a time?"
—Chandra Nalaar
While the root remains, the tree yet lives.
Elmut had slaughtered vampires, slain werewolves, and destroyed hordes of zombies. Sadly, he never got over his fear of spiders.

"Stoke a fire hot enough and you'll never run out of things to burn."
—Xenagos, the Reveler
A single drop turns skin to scale and fist to claw.

"Monsters dwell in every heart. We only think civilization tames them."
—Euphemia, Nexus watcher
Yavimaya lights the quickest path to battle.

"This palace will be our fire-spit, and roasted prince our victory meal. Send in the torch-pigs!"
—Ghut Rak, Gruul guildmage
On the third night, the villagers destroyed their clocks. The sounds of whirring gears and chiming metal held only dread for them.
In the abstract memories of the Iquati, Jace found interesting ideas to improve upon.

"You know it to be false, but when its claws find you, what you know won't matter much at all."
—Pol Jamaar, illusionist
Information travels quickly through Ravnica's network of messengers and thought agents.
What happens when it is the dream that wakes and the sleeper that fades into memory?

"It's as strong as you believe it is, and it's very convincing."
—Jace Beleren
"The secret entrance should be near."
The Dimir would hire her, if only they knew where she lived. The Azorius would condemn her, if only they knew her name.
"The universe is my instrument, and the song I play upon it is one you are forbidden to hear."
"Words of power never disappear. They sleep, awaiting those with the will to rouse them."
Its hunger and ire are no less for being wrought of lies and mist.
"I am who I pretend to be."

"Is the maze itself a phantom? Or is one as real as the other? Perhaps I am as mad as the dragon."
—Jace Beleren, journal

"As you inject the *viscus vitae* into the brain stem, don't let the spastic moaning bother you. It will soon become music to your ears."
—Stitcher Geralf
"Everyone in this city is choosing sides. I choose inside."
"Roil tide! Roil tide! Tie yourselves down!"

"To sculpt a mind is to see every memory and thought as an individual piece that can be rearranged—or removed."
—Jace Beleren
For the Azorius, the law can be a physical shield against chaos and anarchy.
Six feet of earth muffled his cries.

"Beware the seagrafs just off the shore. These waters are filled with hungry geists looking for an easy meal."
—Captain Eberhart
"Heel."

"Do as I think, not as I do."
—Jace Beleren

"I don't need to have the perfect plan. My foe just has to have an imperfect one."
—Jace Beleren
"Brute force can sometimes kick down a locked door, but knowledge is a skeleton key."

"Is the inevitable any less miraculous?"
—Veldka, wandering sage
The last reliable landmark in Tazeem just walked away.

"You can't think your way out of this, Jace. Thought implies life, and life requires a pulse—music to a hunter's ears."
—Vraska
Rakdos cultists are her best customers. They never flinch at pain and are seldom good at math.
Even the lost and undead need a protector.
Every inch of Ravnica is home to something.

"Sheath your swords! Cudgels only. I see a new pair of waterproof trek boots slithering away."
—Nablus, North Hada trapper
It grows to hate you.

"The Golgari would say that life comes from death and death comes from life. But sometimes, death comes from the dead."
—Vraska
"Don't worry. I know the drill."

"Merciless to the point of psychosis. Let's give him a job."
—Zelinas, Orzhov recruiter
Its victims feel only an itchy, wriggling feeling just under their skin. By then, it's far too late.
The Izzet's plans to exploit the undercity ran into a few stubborn obstacles.
The ohran viper is not cold-blooded. Its veins course with the same antigelid venom used to kill its prey.
Those without breath can't complain.

"Bury your dead deep. The boars are hungriest while the corpse is still warm."
—Paulin, trapper of Somberwald
When civilization encroaches on nature, Zendikar encroaches back.
"Tonight, madam, it's your money *and* your life."

"You can't protect them all, Jace."
—Vraska

"The Golgari expand, yes, but I refuse to call their tainted creations 'growth.'"
—Niszka, Selesnya evangel
Linger on death's door and risk being invited in.

"I have seen things that would reduce a weaker person to blubbering and raving. Want to hear about them?"
—Vraska
Gorgons crave beautiful things: gems, exquisite amulets, the alabaster corpses of the petrified dead . . .

"Romanticize it, glamorize it, call it what you will. To me, it will always be carnal, bloody murder."
—Ayli, Kamsa cleric
If you're looking for it, it's available. The question is how much you're willing to pay.

"You are correct. This is going to hurt."
—Vraska

"Watch people flock to a murder scene. Then tell me we're not all a little sick in the head."
—Juri, proprietor of the Juri Revue
Enter those who are starving and sick. You are welcome among the Swarm when the rest of Ravnica rejects you.
Rumors quickly spread among thieves about a labyrinth without walls and a prize beyond all measures of worth.
The upside to not thinking about the consequences is that you'll always surprise those who do.
"Swords, to me! We must engage their line to protect our archers and mages. Let no one fail this task!"
Formerly oppressed by the polis of Meletis, leonin occasionally "mistake" their old enemies for game.
The undead of Grixis are fueled by their hatred of the living.
Every once in a while, when they aren't getting incinerated in lava, crushed under rock slides, or devoured by dragons, goblins experience moments of unmitigated glory in battle.
Don't let him lead the soldiers, but by all means let him lead the way.
Grixis is a world where the only things found in abundance are death and decay. Corpses, whole or in part, are the standard currency among necromancers and demons.
They poured from the Skirk Ridge like lava, burning and devouring everything in their path.
"Those who have never ridden before the wind do not know the true joy of war."
Whether trained, ridden, or eaten, few goblin military innovations have rivaled the bug.

"He displays a perverse charisma fueled by avarice. Highly dangerous. Recommend civil sanctions."
—Agmand Sarv, Azorius hussar
Ogres are driven by passion, rage, and another ogre standing behind them with a whip.
Boros soldiers are like a cache of bombs ready to explode, and the flame-kin light their fuses.
The oni leapt easily from peak to peak, toying with its victims, its voice a purr from the rumbling depths of nightmare.
The climax of a warlord's career is always death.

"The beauty of it is they never see it coming. Ever."
—Razzix, sparkmage
Witches of the Split-Eye Coven speak of a future when Grixis will overflow with life energy. For now, they must harvest vis from the living to fuel their dark magics.

"Don't try to hit your enemies. Concentrate on the space between them, and fill the air with doom."
—Spear-Tribe teaching
With one motion, a pest is removed and a scourge inflicted.
Goblins are eager to follow orders, especially when those orders involve stealing, hurting, annoying, eating, destroying, or swearing.

"Rage courses in every heart, yearning to betray its rational prison."
—Sarkhan Vol

"The people of Akros must learn from our leonin adversaries. If we match their staunch ferocity with our superior faith, we cannot fail."
—Cymede, queen of Akros

"Crispy! Scarback! Load another volcano-ball."
—Stumphobbler Thuj, orcish captain
Jund feasts on the unprepared.
For Sarkhan Vol, the dragon is the purest expression of life's savage splendor.
Without the interfering hands of civilization, nature will always shape itself to its own needs.

"Only the weak imprison themselves behind walls. We live free under the wind, and our freedom makes us strong."
—Zurgo, khan of the Mardu
"Do not concern yourself with my origin, my race, or my ancestry. Seek my record in the pits, and then make your wager."
Many Tin Street shops display a sign on the door: "No cloaks allowed."
They wait in darkened depths, laughing eagerly.
Sparkmages are performance artists of sorts, but pain is the price of admission.
His mission has become a grim pilgrimage, a tour of the Eldrazi-stricken outposts across Zendikar. But he marches on alone, stubborn as the daily dawn.
A skilled decoy can throw your enemies off your trail. A master decoy can survive to do it again.
"For us, a rope represents the ties that bind the kor. For you, it's more literal."

"You think no one is watching, you think you're smart enough to escape, and most foolish of all, you think no one cares."
—Arrester Lavinia, Tenth Precinct
Sudden vengeance, echoing fury.
Small enough to penetrate the narrowest crack in a castle wall and numerous enough to hack apart a griffin.
The first spell taught to young mages, it has spared the lives of many whose hands are too small to hold a sword.

"Having conviction is more important than being righteous."
—Aurelia
"You call it luck. I call it preparation."
The fatal flaw in every plan is the assumption that you know more than your enemy.
Though less well-known than its army of soldiers, the Boros Legion's mage-priests are as respected by the innocent as they are hated by the ghosts of the guilty.
"Forgive me, Master Kami, but in the interest of my people I must halt your advance."
"Do you smell something burning?"
Keranos is a fickle god, delivering punishment as readily as prophecy.

"Your deed cannot be undone. You, however, can be."
—Agosto, Azorius imperator
When asked how many paths reach enlightenment, the monk kicked a heap of sand. "Count," he smiled, "and then find more grains."
Take two steps north into the unsettled future, south into the unquiet past, east into the present day, or west into the great unknown.
"Oathbreaker, I cast you out!"

"You were defeated the moment you declared your aggression."
—Gideon Jura
"The Boros fight for justice. The Azorius fight for law. I hold the line between, and make sure the people are given both."

"The people of Akros must learn from our leonin adversaries. If we match their staunch ferocity with our superior faith, we cannot fail."
—Cymede, queen of Akros

"In our war Heliod gave mortals some favor, yet other times he withheld aid. Are we still no more than game pieces to him?"
—Polyxene the Doubter
Banking steeply, the aven streaked toward the ground—and vanished.

"Our death-arrows flew in high arcs towards the aven. And then . . . nothing."
—Coliseum guard
Entire platoons have mysteriously vanished from battle, leaving enemy weapons to slice through empty air.
They're trained in the art of pressing their luck.
"If a boggart even dares breathe near one of my kin, I'll know. And I'll not be happy."
"Sometimes I snare the unexpected, but I know its purpose will be revealed in time."

"On every plane I've encountered loxodons, I've found stalwart and loyal friends."
—Elspeth

"The southern fortress taken by invaders? Heh, sure . . . when elephants fly."
—Brezard Skeinbow, captain of the guard

"Such deeds should be common fare for such as us."
—Anax, king of Akros
She will not touch a weapon, yet she is the greatest protector her people have ever known.
"In troubled times, we all need someone to watch our back."
Like blinking or breathing, responding to an alarm is an involuntary reflex.

"I was called to this world of steel, and it will be my steel that answers."
—Elspeth

"Bant sentries were called the Angel Line. They never faltered, and they were ready to die defending their position."
—Elspeth

"It's easy for the innocent to speak of justice. They seldom feel its terrible power."
—Orim, Samite inquisitor
"Courage is a proud and gleaming shield. It does not bend or hide from sight. To fight with courage, we must forge in steel."
"Truth is a straight, keen edge. There are no soft angles or rounded edges. To fight for truth, we must forge in steel."

"Learn not only from the failures of the past, but also from its triumphs."
—Isperia
"You can come back once you've learned some manners—and figured out how to reconstitute your physical forms."

"Into its maw went the seventh sea, never to be seen again while the world remains."
—Esper fable

"Beauty to the eye does not always translate to the touch."
—Naimah, Femeref philosopher
Her prophecies amaze her even as she speaks them.
"Soulless demon, you are bound to me. Now we will both dwell in oblivion."
Surrakar grab things they *don't* want.

"I can see why this appeals to Thassa."
—Kiora

"I will never run out of new oceans to explore or new sea-dwellers to embrace as my own."
—Kiora
Torching Krosa would be pointless. It grows faster than it burns.

"Don't be fooled. If it were as docile as it looks, it would've died off long ago."
—Yon Basrel, Oran-Rief survivalist
It's not the two heads you should fear. It's the four fangs.
It is an expert at culling individuals who stray too far from the herd.

"Nature was slowly heading in the right direction, but we know how to achieve faster results."
—Vorel of the Hull Clade
"She may call herself Kiora but I believe she is Thassa, the embodiment of the sea and empress of the depths."

"The enlightenment I never found in etherium I have found traced in the coatl's scales."
—Ranalus, vedalken heretic
The Simic soon discovered that the sky offered as few constraints on size as the sea.

"Everything serves a purpose. Even you."
—Vorel of the Hull Clade

"We've bred out the shortcomings of the species' natural form and replaced them with assets of our own design."
—Momir Vig
As the Simic released more of their krasis experiments, they required new habitats, always at the expense of the locals.
Without the interfering hands of civilization, nature will always shape itself to its own needs.

"When gods become apathetic, the people will worship anyone who answers their pleas."
—Kiora
Once a welcoming hub for explorers, Affa became a place of guarded tongues and quick defenses.
As the hedrons began to coalesce into colossal Eldrazi superstructures, the griffins were forced to seek new territory lest their aeries be crushed between the massive stone monoliths.

"'Invincible' is just a word."
—Gideon Jura
A boon to those who cannot see in the dark. A bane to those who live in it.

"Petrifying gaze, deadly fangs, knifelike dorsal spines, venomous saliva . . . Am I missing anything? . . . Toxic bones? Seriously?"
—Samila, Murasa Expeditionary House
"The elders say Zendikar has no safe, peaceful places. How would they know? They've never looked."
He'll cleave wood and bone alike to carve a path for his allies.

"Don't be fooled. If it were as docile as it looks, it would've died off long ago."
—Yon Basrel, Oran-Rief survivalist
"This world will not be tamed."
The Roil redraws the world as it passes, leaving only the hedrons unchanged.
Adventuring bards recite *Chanter's Epics*, never-ending tales that keep their comrades' minds alert to danger.
Some druids nurture gardens. Others nurture continents.

"Survival rule 781: There are always more scute bugs."
—Zurdi, goblin shortcutter
Its territory is defined by wherever it is at the moment.

"Life as we know it dangles on the brink of extinction. We must show the strength they would steal from us."
—*The Invokers' Tales*
"The shadow travels toward the apex. I predict we will soon see the true measure of darkness."

"We suffer uneasy ground, unstable alliances, and unpredictable magic. Something you can truly trust is worth more than a chest of gold."
—Nikou, Joraga bard
Every world is an organism, able to grow new lands. Some just do it faster than others.
The Eldrazi hunger without limit and consume without pause.
Your pleas for death shall go unheard.

"Whatever the Eldrazi's purpose is, it has nothing to do with something so insignificant as us."
—Nirthu, lone missionary

"The brood lineages unfolded across the world, each patterned after one of three progenitors, each a study in mindless consumption."
—*The Invokers' Tales*
Some humans willingly offered up their blood, hoping it would grant the vampire families the strength to stave off the Eldrazi.
His verdict is always guilty. His sentence is always death.
The mouth must be pried open before rigor mortis sets in. Otherwise the returning soul can find no ingress.

"Others ask why the Eldrazi destroy. I ask why they preserve."
—Ganda, Goma Fada deserter
All the angel saw was her doom.
The dead know lessons the living haven't learned.

"Before I hire new recruits, I test how long they can hold their breath. You'd be surprised how often it comes up."
—Zahr Gada, Halimar expedition leader
Wordlessly it leads its abhorrent brood.

"Play no favorites. Everybody dies."
—Sparkmage saying
Just when you thought you'd be safe, in the middle of an open field with no Eldrazi around for miles.

"The purpose of existence is simple: everything is fuel for the magmaw."
—Jaji, magmaw worshipper
Once thrown, twice burned.

"While we delay, they're on the move. They will not wait as we bicker. We are losing this war by moments as our goal slips beyond our reach."
—Gideon Jura
What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?
Scholars had puzzled for centuries over the ruins at Tal Terig. Its secrets had always lived within one rune-carved head.
Each temple is a door to a horrible future.

"What cannot be destroyed will be bound."
—Oath of Avacyn
"Evil will soon be vanquished. What Innistrad most needs now is healing."
"I stand for every cobbler, tanner, and fool in this town—and they stand for me."
Death has bound it with chains of past regrets. Forever it searches for atonement, each kindness removing a single link.

"Never forget our ancestors. They have not forgotten us."
—Mikaeus, the Lunarch
He vowed he would never rest until he reached his destination. He doesn't know how right he was.
The barrier between existence and oblivion is thinner than you know.
"My greatest hope is that you will surpass me in every way, consigning my name to some forgotten corner of history."
"You have done your best. I give you leave to rest."
In the memories of those they lost lies the strength needed to defend their city.
The Host sings of Avacyn's return without a single verse about its own suffering.
Inquisitors are taught scripture, philosophy, and the fine art of sharpening an axe.

"No one chooses to be stitched together into a skaab. If it could speak, it would beg for its own destruction."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar
You don't want to see his trophy room.
"Let them decry me for burning the dead. I'm not giving those ghoulcallers any more fuel for their madness."
"Priests, hunters, slayers—to arms! The enemy approaches!"
Her horn is heard across Innistrad, lifting the hearts of the righteous.
"I am no mere ship's captain. The north wind is my accomplice. The tide is my first mate."

"Ghouls smashed the door, but I heard the call of the gryffs and knew we were saved."
—Ekka, shopkeeper of Hanweir

"When you see a raven, head for the hills. It knows when the ghost-tide is headed in."
—Sved, fisherman of Nephalia
"My drivers are trustworthy. I removed their tongues myself. Any other questions?"
"'I'm certain that the fate of Markov Manor is connected to these cryptoliths . . .' This Tamiyo was on to something."
Jenrik's tower is served by those who once sought to enter it uninvited.
Outside the safety of Thraben, there is little distinction between tool and weapon.
Not everyone can have a sword of blessed silver. Not everyone needs one, either.
"So much for neighborly hospitality!"
"So many corpses, so little time."

"It always amazes me what perfectly good things people throw away."
—Ludevic, necro-alchemist

"The cathars killed my skaabs down below. Let's see how high their swords can reach."
—Ludevic, necro-alchemist
Its screeching is the sound of you losing your mind.

"The best skaabs are more powerful and more beautiful than the sum of their parts."
—Stitcher Geralf
Death took his humanity but not his skill with the knife.
Just as with a peach, the first bite is always the juiciest.

"We must all make sacrifices for the good of Innistrad."
—Sorin Markov
Without a mind, it doesn't fear death. Without a soul, it doesn't mind killing.

"At least this one still has arms and legs. Well, most of its legs."
—Enslow, ghoulcaller of Nephalia
The will to return can overpower the will to survive.
Some vampires resorted to corpse trading after cathars burned their estates and drove them from their ancestral feeding grounds.
"I often think on how excited they must feel to be chosen as my prey."

"Come. Bring your brothers. Tonight, you feast on living flesh."
—Jadar, ghoulcaller of Nephalia

"Innistrad's ghoulcallers are talented enough, but let me show you what someone with real power can create."
—Liliana Vess

"He is judge, jury, and executioner because he killed them all."
—Bishop Cawle of Elgaud

"I have seen a hundred mortal families rise and fall. I shall outlast a thousand more."
—Olivia Voldaren
For a ghoul, every village is a buffet and every disaster is a reunion.
Marella was delighted. The ball had attracted so many suitors for her daughter, including that handsome stranger. She wondered where the two were now . . . .

"Do not touch a drop. Not yet. I want to watch this so-called slayer's last crisis of faith."
—Olivia Voldaren
Though its mind has long since rotted away, it wields a sword with deadly skill.
For the necro-alchemist, any puzzle can be solved with intelligence and harvested body parts.
They seek out living trees to glean age-old secrets from sap and wood.
"These alleys are not safe. Come, I can guide you back to the market square."
Zendikar's elves have developed innovative methods to mitigate the effects of the Roil.
"From a tiny sprout, the greatest trees grow and flourish. May the seeds of your mind be equally fruitful."
Desmera blinded her seers so that her beauty would be the last image burned in their memories. The act only deepened their insight.
Nature's arms encircle all who are willing to draw close.
"Zendikar will not surrender, and neither can we."
Once, Nissa selected worthy fighters to defend the Joraga. Now, she gathers forces to defend all of Zendikar.
"Roam as you will, your roots remain in the strong earth of your Rising."

"The world was not hostile to us—we were beneath its notice, and presented no danger."
—*The Invokers' Tales*

"A good lagac will carry you through thick and thin. A bad one . . . well, it's a tasty dinner."
—Raff Slugeater, goblin shortcutter
Eldrazi are not the leopard's preferred prey, but they are better than no prey at all.

"The horizon is the perpetual ideal, the constant promise of hope."
—Nissa Revane
Their arrows are tipped with basilisk eyes and fletched with cockatrice feathers.
"The most elegant solutions are found in nature. You just have to know where to look."
Through the waves of Eldrazi attacks, the Murasan jungles seemed to regrow as soon as they were destroyed.
It carries the hopes of Zendikar's embattled wilds on its mighty boughs.

"I will secure my revenge on Zendikar one soul at a time."
—Ob Nixilis

"Conquering your first world is the hardest, after all. My power grew as I moved from world to world, taking anything that would make the next taking easier."
